chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu'l Khattab narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alawi, from his father Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abu Talib, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon him).
He said: I asked the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) about the man who sleeps and then sees a dream -- sometimes it is true and sometimes it is false.

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: O Ali! There is no servant who sleeps except that his spirit is raised toward the Lord of the worlds. Whatever he sees in the presence of the Lord of the worlds is truth. Then, when God, the Mighty, the Omnipotent, commands the return of his spirit to his body, and the spirit is between heaven and earth, whatever it sees then are confused dreams.

key_terms.أضغاث أحلام: Confused/tangled dreams (adghath ahlam), a Quranic expression for meaningless dreams
key_terms.الرؤيا: Dream or vision (ru'ya), particularly one seen during sleep
key_terms.رب العالمين: Lord of the worlds (Rabb al-Alamin), God as sustainer of all creation
key_terms.عرج بروحه: His spirit is raised/ascended (mi'raj of the soul during sleep)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic explanation for why some dreams are true and some are false?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition from al-Amali of al-Saduq, Imam Ali (AS) recounts asking the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) about the nature of dreams. The Prophet explained that during sleep, the human spirit ascends to God, and what it perceives there is true vision. However, during the descent back to the body, when the spirit is between heaven and earth, its perceptions become confused dreams (adghath ahlam). This cosmological teaching was imparted privately to Ali and provides an Islamic framework for understanding the difference between veridical and false dreams.
